question: What is the main difference between a communicable disease and a non-communicable disease?

options.A: It cannot be treated with standard medications
options.B: It is always caused by a genetic mutation
options.C: It only affects people living in urban areas
options.D: It can be transmitted from a reservoir to a susceptible host

explanation: You've got this! Communicable diseases can spread from one person or source to another, unlike chronic conditions like hypertension.

question: When managing an infectious disease, why should a community nurse look beyond just the individual patient?

options.A: Because individual treatments are rarely effective against infections
options.B: To comply with hospital administrative discharge policies
options.C: To prevent the illness from spreading to other members of the community
options.D: Because infectious agents only survive outside the human body

explanation: Great thinking! In community health, we treat the patient while also protecting the wider population from an outbreak.

question: Through which route does a pathogen typically leave a human body?

options.D: White blood cells in the bone marrow

explanation: Spot on! Pathogens love to hitch a ride out of the body through fluids, mucus, cough droplets, or open skin sores.

question: Why is the chain of infection a helpful tool for nurses?

options.A: It determines the financial cost of treating an infectious outbreak
options.B: It proves whether an infection is bacterial or viral in origin
options.C: It shows where interventions can break the cycle and stop transmission
options.D: It helps nurses calculate the exact incubation period of a virus

explanation: Exactly! By seeing how the links connect, you know exactly where to step in with handwashing or vaccines to stop the spread.

question: Which of the following is an example of vector-borne transmission?

options.A: Inhaling respiratory droplets from someone coughing nearby
options.B: A mosquito transmitting the malaria parasite to a human
options.C: Drinking water contaminated with cholera bacteria
options.D: Acquiring a skin infection through direct contact with a sore

explanation: Vectors are living organisms, most commonly insects, that carry and transmit infectious pathogens to humans. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T1#GNS313_U2_T1_h3)

question: A patient falls ill with typhoid after drinking contaminated water. What type of transmission is this?
explanation: You got it! Because the water acted as a vehicle between the source and the patient, it counts as indirect transmission.

question: What goes on inside the body during the incubation period of an infection?

options.A: The patient experiences severe, disease-specific symptoms
options.B: The body completely eliminates the infectious agent
options.C: The host is fully recovered and no longer contagious
options.D: The pathogen multiplies inside the host before symptoms appear

explanation: Well done! The incubation period is that quiet window of time between catching the germ and first feeling sick.

question: What is the classic sign that a patient has entered the prodromal stage of an infection?

options.A: Vague feelings of tiredness and mild body discomfort
options.B: Sudden appearance of distinct, textbook skin rashes
options.C: Full-blown paralysis of the lower extremities
options.D: Complete recovery of normal daily energy levels

explanation: That's it! The prodromal stage is when the patient just feels 'off' or unusually tired before the main symptoms show up.

question: What is the primary vector responsible for transmitting Lassa fever in endemic regions?
explanation: Lassa fever is primarily transmitted to humans through contact with food or items contaminated by infected multimammate rodents. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T1#GNS313_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why do waterborne diseases like cholera often spike during the rainy season in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Rainfall increases the population of adult malaria-carrying mosquitoes
options.B: Cold weather lowers overall human immunity against intestinal parasites
options.C: Heavy rains can wash surface waste and sewage into vulnerable drinking water sources
options.D: Humidity causes airborne bacteria to multiply rapidly in closed indoor spaces

explanation: Exactly right. Heavy floods easily mix surface waste into community water supplies, increasing the risk of waterborne illnesses.

question: Why is epidemiological surveillance so important in community health?

options.A: To monitor disease trends and detect outbreaks early
options.B: To diagnose individual patients with chronic ailments
options.C: To design new pharmaceutical drugs in laboratories
options.D: To calculate monthly salaries for hospital staff members

explanation: You nailed it! Surveillance helps public health teams track disease patterns so they can catch and stop outbreaks early.

question: As a nurse, what should you do when you encounter a notifiable disease?

options.A: Treating the patient at home without informing the clinic director
options.B: Promptly reporting confirmed or suspected cases to public health authorities
options.C: Keeping the diagnosis strictly confidential from government agencies
options.D: Waiting until a laboratory test is 100 percent certain before acting

explanation: Correct! Reporting notifiable diseases helps health departments jump into action and protect the wider community.

question: Which of these nursing actions is an example of primary prevention?

options.A: Screening adults for high blood pressure at a clinic
options.B: Tracing contacts of a patient with active tuberculosis
options.C: Providing physical therapy after a stroke
options.D: Administering routine vaccines to healthy children

explanation: Brilliant! Primary prevention stops a disease before it even starts—like giving immunizations to healthy kids.

question: A healthy family member who was exposed to measles is asked to stay at home and avoid contact with others for a short period. What is this control measure called?
explanation: You got it! Quarantine is used for healthy people who were exposed, to watch if they develop symptoms, whereas isolation is for people who are already sick.
